report.summary: Chunk 7 of 15 for correctness.py: contains apply_patch, Selection dataclass, freeze_selection, and start of _check_selection. All claims checked.

handoff.purpose: Provides apply_patch, Selection dataclass, freeze_selection, and start of _check_selection.

symbols.name: apply_patch
symbols.note: Applies patch bytes to worktree via git apply; returns None on success, error string on failure.

symbols.name: Selection
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding the immutable selection of test nodes, base revision, overlay, gate, and timeout. Provides digest property.

symbols.name: Selection.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict representation of selection, includes argv_shape and digest.

symbols.name: Selection.digest
symbols.note: SHA256 hex digest of the selection's content (first 16 chars).

symbols.name: freeze_selection
symbols.note: Builds a Selection from a task dict and base_revision. Deduplicates and sorts node ids.

symbols.name: _check_selection
symbols.note: Starts here; signature and partial implementation. Purpose: validate selection consistency? (incomplete in chunk)

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a ``could_not_run``, never a ``not_fixed``
claims.why: The docstring explains the semantics but the actual classification (could_not_run vs not_fixed) is not present in this chunk; it would be used elsewhere.

claims.text: ``digest`` covers all of it. Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes
claims.why: The digest property serializes all fields (base_revision, fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, test_revision, test_overlay, gate, timeout_s) and hashes them; any change alters the digest.

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so "what was measured is what was declared" is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring.
claims.why: The class is decorated with @dataclass(frozen=True) and fields are typed as tuples (tuple[str, ...]), ensuring immutability.

claims.text: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem.
claims.why: The function uses dict.fromkeys to deduplicate while preserving order, then sorts; it does no filesystem access, expansion, or filtering.

claims.text: this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: This claim refers to the entire codebase; cannot confirm/deny based on this chunk alone.

observations.what: apply_patch returns None on success and a string reason on failure; docstring says 'Returns None, or the reason.'
apply_patch uses a temporary file to hold patch bytes and deletes it in a finally block.
Selection.digest uses hashlib.sha256, truncates to 16 hex characters (64 bits).
freeze_selection sorts node id tuples after deduplication via dict.fromkeys (which preserves insertion order in Python 3.7+).
_check_selection is defined but only its signature appears; the implementation is cut off at end of chunk.
